heads.la: TITULI CANTICI CANTICORUM EXPLICATIO. Titulus autem hujus operis est: Cantica canticorum Salomonis.
heads.en: EXPLANATION OF THE TITLE OF THE SONG OF SONGS. Now the title of this work is: Songs of songs of Solomon.

headnotes.la: … nardo, sine altera specie vel mistura, fit unguentum laudabile et confectio profutura; et Maria Magdalena pedes Domini ungere voluit hoc unguento, sicut satis innotuit lectionis evangelicae documento
headnotes.en: …a laudable ointment and a confection that shall profit; and Mary Magdalene willed to anoint the Lord's feet with this ointment, as hath been made sufficiently known by the witness of the gospel lesson

headnotes.la: …et devoti, qui ad tantam gratiam contribulato spiritu sunt promoti, ut ungant pedes Jesu, et ad caput ipsum profectu veniant ampliore, et nares circumstantium, vel potius totam domum repleant ex odore
headnotes.en: …dvanced to so great a grace that they anoint the feet of Jesus, and by a fuller progress come to the head itself, and fill the nostrils of them that stand by, or rather the whole house, with the odour

headnotes.la: Et supra in hoc epithalamio
headnotes.en: And above in this epithalamium

headnotes.la: …n: (Eccles. VII)], adest statim cinnamomum, quod colore, cineri similatur: monens ut in omnibus ad quae profectu congruo meretur sapiens proficisci, quis, unde, quo perveniat nunquam desinat reminisci
headnotes.en: … colour is made like to ashes; admonishing that in all things whereunto by a fitting advance the wise man deserveth to go forward, he never cease to call to mind who, and whence, and whither he cometh

headnotes.la: Et Job
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Gen. 3:19 *pulvis es, et in pulverem reverteris*, "dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return."] And Job

headnotes.la: …ffectu et effectu prospero se suspendit, in hoc tamen excellenti fastigio cinerem se attendit, ostendens de oblato sic beneficio se gaudere, ut sua digne memorans, videatur quasi de proprio nil audere
headnotes.en: …that excellent height he marked himself to be ashes, showing that he so rejoiced in the benefit offered him that, duly remembering what was his own, he seemed as it were to dare nothing out of his own

headnotes.la: …on enim labor per amorem, sed amor per laborem, quasi visibilem se ostentat, ideo myrrha prius nominatur, quae praedux et praevia primitus vult videri, munere cujus amor meretur cognoscibilis exhiberi
headnotes.en: …ve through labour showeth itself as it were visible; and therefore myrrh is named first, which willeth to be seen first as guide and forerunner, by whose gift love deserveth to be shown forth knowable

headnotes.la: …tmodum aloe nominatur, eo scilicet quod voluntas jam visibili opere demonstratur; et in unam misturam in oculis recte credentium convenerunt, quo conventu nostris doloribus unguentum utile confecerunt
headnotes.en: …ll is now shown forth by a visible work; and in the eyes of them that rightly believe they came together into one mixture, by which coming together they compounded an ointment profitable for our pains

headnotes.la: et
headnotes.en: and

headnotes.la: … innuit Christum in pondere et numero suum nobis beneficium contulisse; et quod ante fuerat verbis et significationibus transitoriis prophetatum, tandem esse certo pondere, perfecto numero consummatum
headnotes.en: …rist bestowed his benefit upon us in weight and number; and that what had before been prophesied in transitory words and significations was at last consummated in a certain weight and a perfect number

headnotes.la: …tatur, quia sicut Pater Spiritum, sic et Filius mittere se testatur, qui spiritus etsi ubi vult, et quando vult, adesse creditur, et prodesse, ab eo tamen mittitur, cum quo habet naturaliter unum esse
headnotes.en: …e Son testifieth that he sendeth the Spirit, which spirit, although he is believed to be present where he will and when he will, and to profit, yet is sent by him with whom he hath naturally one being

headnotes.la: …nt, non fatentur, quid nisi caput ejus gravare et offendere non verentur, tantisque illud gravaminibus et molestiis adimplere, ut laborem tam plenarium quasi non valeat sustinere? Unde per Isaiam Deus
headnotes.en: …d, the Son of God, what do they but fear not to burden and to offend his head, and to fill it with so great burdens and vexations that he can as it were not bear so full a labour? Whence God by Isaias
